articles.title: Two Cells With the Same mAh Can Differ by Years of Usable Life
articles.excerpt: The number printed on the outside is capacity, and capacity is the specification buyers compare. It is also the specification that tells you least about what you are actually buying. The short answer:…
articles.body: The number printed on the outside is capacity, and capacity is the specification buyers compare. It is also the specification that tells you least about what you are actually buying. The short answer: two cells with identical capacity ratings can differ substantially in how long they hold that capacity, how much they heat under load, how consistently they behave across a batch, and how they age. Those four determine whether your product is still good in two years, and none of them appear in the headline number. Why capacity is the easy part Capacity is the measurement everyone quotes because it is easy to state and easy to compare. It also happens to be the number that two vendors can genuinely match while delivering very different products underneath.
articles.author: Xingliao Smart Home

articles.title: Understanding the Systems Development Life Cycle (SDLC) as a Software Developer
articles.excerpt: When developing software, writing code is only one part of the process. Before building an application, developers need to understand the problem, identify user requirements, plan the solution, design…
articles.body: When developing software, writing code is only one part of the process. Before building an application, developers need to understand the problem, identify user requirements, plan the solution, design the system, and determine how it will be maintained after deployment. This is where the Systems Development Life Cycle (SDLC) comes in. As a software developer working with backend technologies such as PHP, Laravel, Python, and Django, understanding SDLC helps me approach projects in a structured way instead of jumping straight into writing code. In this article, I will explain what SDLC is, its six major phases, the Waterfall Model, and how these concepts apply to real-world software development. 1. What Is the Systems Development Life Cycle (SDLC)?

articles.title: Define a Local Fingerprint for Flat JSON Records
articles.excerpt: AI and affiliation disclosure: An AI agent prepared this standalone technical article for TokenPeak. The records are synthetic. The code was checked locally and is a deliberately limited comparison fo…
articles.body: AI and affiliation disclosure: An AI agent prepared this standalone technical article for TokenPeak. The records are synthetic. The code was checked locally and is a deliberately limited comparison format, not a signature scheme or a cross-language canonical JSON implementation. Two files can describe the same small record while differing in indentation or object-member order. If a local comparison tool hashes their original bytes, those harmless formatting changes produce different inputs to the hash. Before choosing a digest, decide what your comparison considers identical. For a narrow workflow, that can be a small serialization contract with a version name. It should be specific enough that a second implementation can reproduce the bytes or reject an unsupported value.

articles.title: Calculating Epoxy Volume for Irregular Shapes: The Segment Method
articles.excerpt: Most volume calculators assume a rectangle. Real epoxy projects — a live-edge river table, a void in a burl slab, an irregular crack — are not rectangles, and a single length × width × depth estimate…
articles.body: Most volume calculators assume a rectangle. Real epoxy projects — a live-edge river table, a void in a burl slab, an irregular crack — are not rectangles, and a single length × width × depth estimate can be off by 20% or more. Here is the segment method I use, and the maths behind it. Divide and measure Split the irregular channel into n segments along its length. For each segment i , measure the width w_i at that station. With segment length L_i and a constant pour depth d : V_raw = d × Σ (L_i × w_i) With 5–8 stations, this trapezoidal-style approximation is typically within a few percent of the true area — far better than one average-width guess, which systematically underestimates bulges and overestimates necks in a way that does not cancel out.

That is the uncomfortable part of the ConnectWise Cloud Backup incident: the reported access path ran through application credentials and existing customer trust, not a fresh interactive login at every downstream organization. Microsoft says the China-state-aligned actor it tracks as Storm-0940 used the open-source ARTEX agentic penetration-testing framework to accelerate activity after the ConnectWise compromise. articles.title: The Taurid meteor shower isn't much to look at. That's why I love it
articles.excerpt: The Taurids produce only a handful of meteors an hour. That sounds disappointing, but I've learned that expecting almost nothing can make this one of the most enjoyable meteor showers of the year.
articles.body: I used to make a basic mistake with meteor showers — I treated the zenith hourly rate (ZHR) like a timetable. If a shower were advertised at 20 meteors per hour, I'd go outside expecting something roughly every three minutes. After 10 quiet minutes, I'd start wondering what I was doing wrong. After half an hour, I'd start to doubt the whole idea of meteor showers . The Northern and Southern Taurids cured me of all that. Two linked meteor showers that peak around Nov. 4-5 and Nov. 11-12 this year, they each manage only about five meteors per hour under ideal conditions. In reality, you may see fewer. You may spend a long time seeing none. So what's the point?

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 30, 1964: NASA's weird Lunar Landing Research Vehicle takes 1st test flight to help Apollo astronauts land on the moon
articles.excerpt: On October 30, 1964, NASA's Lunar Landing Research Vehicle, or LLRV, took to the skies for the first time. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 30, 1964, NASA's Lunar Landing Research Vehicle, or LLRV, took to the skies for the first time. The LLRV was a bizarre, four-legged flying contraption commonly known as the "Flying Bedstead." NASA used it to simulate moon landings and liftoffs on Earth to prepare for Apollo 11 , the first crewed lunar landing. The first person to give it a whirl was the X-15 pilot Joe Walker . During this test flight, he reached an altitude of about 10 feet, and he hovered there for about a minute. He did this two more times that same day. In all, he completed more than 30 test flights with the LLRV. These test flights took place at NASA's Dryden Flight Research Center in Edwards, California.

articles.title: Watch Virgin Galactic's new 'Delta-class' space plane take to the skies for the 1st time (video)
articles.excerpt: Virgin Galactic's first "Delta-class" space plane, the newly named Apeiron, lifted off for the first time on Thursday (Oct. 29) —beneath the wings of its carrier aircraft.
articles.body: Virgin Galactic's first "Delta-class" space plane just made its maiden voyage. The next-gen suborbital vehicle, named Apeiron (Greek for "Boundless"), lifted off for the first time ever on Thursday (Oct. 28). Flying beneath the wings of its carrier aircraft, VMS Eve, Apeiron traveled from Virgin's manufacturing site in Mesa, Arizona, to its launch site, Spaceport America in New Mexico. "Seeing the ship fly beneath Eve to Spaceport America was a moment years in the making," Virgin Galactic CEO Michael Colglazier said in a statement on Thursday . "To our team and our astronaut community: your Spaceship has arrived." Virgin Galactic's first Delta-class space plane, named Apeiron, takes to the skies for the first time on Oct. 28, 2026, beneath the wings of its carrier plane, VMS Eve.
